paper_metadata.title: Fabrication of a novel magnetic high entropy alloy with desirable mechanical properties by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering

evidence.quote: In this study, a novel magnetic CoCuFeMnNi high entropy alloy (HEA) was synthesized using mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS).
Tribological investigations were performed on the CoCuFeMnNi HEA sintered at 850 ◦ C.

process_steps.output_state: CoCuFeMnNi HEA powder with FCC solid solution structure, average crystallite size about 21 nm

evidence.quote: The CoCuFeMnNi HEA powder with FCC solid solution structure and average crystallite size of about 21 nm was successfully synthesized after 50 h mechanical alloying of elemental powders.

process_steps.output_state: CoCuFeMnNi HEA bulk sample with 97 % relative density

evidence.quote: The CoCuFeMnNi HEA bulk sample with the highest relative density of 97 % was fabricated by SPS at the temperature of 850 ◦ C for 8 min under an applied pressure of 40 MPa.
As the milling time reached up to 50 h, the diffraction peaks indicated no alteration except for a slight broadening.
The XRD patterns of SPSed samples at different temperatures are similar, indicating a single-phase FCC solid solution.
It is realized that the sintering temperature of 750 ◦C was not enough to attain a fully dense CoCuFeMnNi HEA bulk alloy (with 9.7 % porosity).

As seen, the relative density enhanced and reached about 97 % when the sintering temperature increased from 750 ◦C to 850 ◦C. Densification improvement at higher temperatures is due to the amelioration in diffusion bonding at particle boundaries, consequently activating other diffusivity paths at higher temperatures [53].
Hence, the number of porosities rose slightly ( Fig. 7 c).
The CoCuFeMnNi HEA powder with FCC solid solution structure and average crystallite size of about 21 nm was successfully synthesized after 50 h mechanical alloying of elemental powders.
